 Nagar.

Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Anish Dayal

Pursuant to the order dated previous order of this Court 15th December, 2022 and 28th February,
2023 despite directions there is no one appearing for respondent No. 2.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the mater has already been settled by settlement dated 04th July, 2017 arrived at with the facilitation of the Mediation Centre Saket Courts.
A perusal of this settlement agreement would show that an amount of Rs. 90,000/- had to be paid by the petitioner to Mr. Lal S. Vaswani in relation to the said matter.
3. The petitioner who appears in person is identified by the counsel and the IO, confirms that this amount has duly paid.
This fact is also recorded in para 7 of the order dated 19th July, 2017 passed by Ld. ASJ, South District, Saket.
4. Further, an order of 23rd September, 2017 was passed by learned MM stating that in view of the settlement, the parties were at liberty to move the petition for quashing before this Court.
It has already noted that Mr. Vaswani has since passed away.
The petitioner also undertakes and confirms that she has not made any other complaint against Mr. Lal S. Vaswani who is now deceased and or his family members, in any manner whatsoever.
5. In view of the above, the statement as well as settlement of the record between the parties.

6. Considering the above settlement between the parties and the chances of conviction of the petitioners being remote and bleak, there is no use continuing with proceedings of the present FIR as it would be a misuse of the process of the Court and an unnecessary burden on the State Jyoti Samtani & Anr vs State (Nct Of Delhi) & Anr on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162265224/
1 exchequer.
